title: Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Sanhedrin 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.25a.13) they said: “What are pigeon-flyers? Here they explain it ‘if your pigeon precedes my pigeon.’ Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya said: Ara.” Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads: “Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya said in Rav’s name.”

Hyman also cites [Bereshit Rabbah 7:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.7.5) and [Bereshit Rabbah 25:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.25.1), and Tanchuma, Shoftim 7. He quotes the saying, “A person whose eye hurts pays a physician,” etc. [Ketubot 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.105a.15) attributes this saying to Rabbi Abbahu. Hyman suggests he may have been a son of Rabbi Oshaya Rabbah, named for his grandfather Rabbi Chama bar Bisa.[^1]

notes.text: [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sanhedrin.25a.13.2) explains ara as using a trained pigeon to lure away other birds. The two Bereshit Rabbah passages name Chama bar Hoshaya on other subjects. The consulted [Tanchuma, Shoftim 7](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma%2C_Shoftim.7.1) gives a different discussion of justice and names Chama bar Chanina. The physician comparison is explicit in Ketubot. Hyman’s apparatus report and proposed ancestry remain his.
